title: customer-escalation-war-room-lumina-health-2026-03-27
content:
Purpose:
Prepare for war-room with Lumina Health (priority customer) to triage elevated token latency and timeouts observed between 03/25 22:30 UTC and ongoing. This doc is meeting prep + live notes + follow-up action items.

Attendees (expected):
- Aisha Martinez (owner, CS lead)
- Ethan Zhao (SRE on-call)
- Priya Kapoor (Serving runtime eng)
- Samir Patel (Solutions Eng)
- Jordan Lee (Customer network/security)
- Lumina contacts: Maya R. (platform), Raul V. (app lead)

Meeting goals (30-45m total):
1) Align on current customer impact and scope (timing, affected routes).
2) Confirm mitigation steps in flight and responsibilities.
3) Decide immediate rollback/fallback or capacity bump plan.
4) Capture action items with owners and SLAs.
5) Agree on customer comms cadence and postmortem owner.

Background / What Lumina reported:
- Points: increased 95th/99th token latency and intermittent request timeouts for model-route "gpt-open-2.7b-quant" used on /v1/generate-chat-route.
- Reported first detection: 2026-03-25 22:33 UTC; traffic spike tied to nightly batch scoring (7x normal token/sec).
- Errors observed: HTTP 504 on ~3% of requests, long tail latencies up to 12s per response (normal baseline 200-400ms per token).
- Customer severity: P1 for Lumina (revenue-impacting).

Immediate context (what we've seen so far):
- Autoscaling triggers: Dedicated pool scaled up 2x at 22:35 UTC; scaling completed 22:43 UTC.
- Routing fallback: system attempted fallback to quantized variant, but KV cache warmup caused extra latency for long-context sessions.
- Observability: token-level breakdown shows high time in attention kernels on GPU nodes with mixed CPU/GPU memory pressure alerts.
- SRE notes: occasional CUDA driver warnings reported on node g-13; not yet fatal.

Pre-meeting checklist (items to confirm before war-room start):
- [Aisha] Confirm customer contact details + confirm they can join at 14:00 PT. (DONE 03/26 09:12 PT)
- [Ethan] Capture current on-call logs and attach tail of /var/log/serving-runtime/* (running).
- [Priya] Snapshot current model config and quantization flags for gpt-open-2.7b-quant.
- [Samir] Collect last 30m of request ids and sample payloads for reproduction.
- [Jordan] Verify there are no recent firewall/network policy changes on Lumina side.

Suggested agenda (30-45m):
0) Quick intro + goal alignment (2m) - Aisha
1) Customer impact summary (5m) - Lumina rep / Aisha
2) Technical summary from SRE & serving runtime (8m) - Ethan / Priya
   - Autoscaling timeline
   - Node health (driver warnings, mem/cpu/gpu usage)
   - Cache warming behavior observed
3) Mitigations in flight & short-term options (10m) - Samir
   - Option A: Force-fallback to smaller non-quant variant (tradeoff: cost/latency)
   - Option B: Increase dedicated pool by N GPU nodes (need infra approval)
   - Option C: Route Lumina traffic to standby region (if cross-region allowed)
4) Customer comms and next steps (5m) - Aisha
5) Assign action items + SLAs (5m)
6) Quick sync time for follow-up (2m)

Live notes (to be filled during meeting) - leave bullets for copy/paste: 
- Customer confirms burst from batch job ID: lumina-batch-20260325-22 (Maya)
- Observed error trace sample request_id=inc-req-00012345 -> timeout at 00:12:34Z
- Node g-13 had repeated driver warning: "CUDA_WARN_PERSISTENT_COPY" at 22:34 and 22:37
- Sampling of 10 requests: 8 show token computation spike during attention phase (token 512-1024)
- Autoscaler logs: scale_up triggered by queue length threshold, but new nodes reported slow boot due to docker image pull (registry throttling)

Immediate mitigation decisions (consensus):
- DO: Temporarily route Lumina traffic to model variant "gpt-open-2.7b-fp16" in region us-west-2 for low-latency paths. (Owner: Samir)
  - Rationale: FP16 variant avoids quantization-induced KV cache warmups and has stable kernel path.
  - Risk: Higher per-token cost; notify billing & customer.
- DO NOT: Roll back to non-quant globally until we validate latency/regression on small traffic.
- DO: Spin up 4 extra warm nodes in dedicated pool as hot spare (Owner: Ethan; ETA: 25m).
- DO: Create temporary rate-limit protection to reduce batch job burst hitting real-time routes (Owner: Priya; ETA: 40m).

Action items (post-meeting):
- Samir Patel: Implement immediate route change to gpt-open-2.7b-fp16 for Lumina; verify sampling on 50 requests. Due: 2026-03-27T15:30Z. (linked: JIRA-INC-9876#comment-1)
- Ethan Zhao: Provision 4 warm nodes in dedicated pool + verify CUDA driver stability; collect /var/log/syslog and dmesg for g-13. Due: 2026-03-27T15:00Z.
- Priya Kapoor: Deploy temporary rate-limiter rule on route /v1/generate-chat-route to cap batch-triggered concurrency to 20. Due: 2026-03-27T15:20Z.
- Jordan Lee: Confirm there was no network ACL change on Lumina side and share network logs (or confirm false). Due: 2026-03-27T16:00Z.
- Aisha Martinez: Draft customer update email (high-level, non-technical) and schedule next check-in at 16:00 PT. Due: 2026-03-27T14:45Z.
- All: Save a copy of sample failing request payloads to the incident folder (CONFLUENCE-1234/attachments). Due: 2026-03-27T15:00Z.

Notes / Questions to follow-up in postmortem:
- Why did node g-13 report driver warnings during scale-up? (Priya + Ethan to investigate)
- Why did autoscaler not prefer cold-started GPU images from our warm pool? (Infra)
- Could cache-warmup behavior be mitigated by on-deploy warmup or per-session pre-warm heuristics? (Serving runtime)
- Do we need an explicit fallback policy for quantized -> fp16 variants in routing layer? (Product + Runtime)

Customer comms template (Aisha):
Hi Maya / Raul -
Thanks for joining the war-room. Short update: we have identified a burst during your nightly scoring job that caused cache warmup + node pressure, which increased latencies for some requests. We are routing you to an FP16 variant as a temporary mitigation and provisioning additional capacity. We will follow up with a detailed timeline and postmortem within 48 hours.

Raw links / artifacts referenced during meeting:
- Incident ticket: JIRA-INC-9876
- Runbook: CONFLUENCE-1234
- Sample logs: slack://archives/CPROD/p12345678
- Registry pull throttling alert: alerts://registry-throttle-2026-03-25

Post-meeting follow-up plan:
- 1 hour check: confirm route change stable and error rate <1% (Ethan + Samir)
- 4 hour postmortem draft: include timeline, root cause hypotheses, and remediation plan (Priya owner)
- Customer postmortem: coordinate with Lumina and legal for any contractual notices (Aisha)

Notes-to-self / scratchpad (informal):
- Reproduce locally: try using lumina batch payload (id lumina-batch-20260325-22) against fp16 variant to measure per-token latency.
- Ping infra on standby node image pre-pull to remediate registry throttling next time.
- Add a short blurb in runbook about "quantized variant warmup" behavior.

Status log (update after meeting):
- 2026-03-27T14:12Z - War-room started. Route change in progress. Samir reports 20/50 sample requests improved.
- 2026-03-27T14:45Z - Ethan reports extra nodes provisioned and healthy; driver warnings not reproduced after node reboot.
- 2026-03-27T15:10Z - Priya applied rate-limiter; batch job re-run shows reduced concurrency.
- 2026-03-27T16:05Z - Customer confirmed degraded experience mitigated; follow-up postmortem assigned.

Next artifacts to produce:
- Incident timeline + metrics export (Priya)
- Postmortem draft (Priya)
- Customer-facing summary (Aisha)

End of doc.
